name: text-3d-flip

frames.best_why: Several letters are caught mid-flip at different angles, the effect at its most visible.

tagline: Letters pivot in 3D one after another when the pointer arrives.
summary: A headline whose letters spring through a 3D flip in a stagger, starting from the first, last, centre or a random glyph, around the axis you choose.
appearance: Two left-aligned lines on black: a bold white headline and a smaller grey subheading. Each glyph has its own slot, and while animating some turn edge-on and show a mirrored back face before snapping upright.
behaviour: Moving the pointer into the text sets every letter flipping around the chosen axis in a cascade, each springing back to face forward over a few tenths of a second. The sequence runs once per entry and never overlaps itself.
demo_content: The lines "Hover to Flip" and "3D Typography"
search_phrases: letters flip around in 3d on hover
text that flips over on mouse over
use_when: A short bold headline should answer the pointer with something more tactile than a colour shift.
avoid_when: Long or small text, where flipped glyphs hurt reading, and touch screens where hover never fires.
customise: The words are children and the wrapper element is as; rotation axis, stagger origin, stagger spacing, spring transition and class names for both faces are props.
weight_why: One span per character with a spring transform on hover, idle the rest of the time.

a11y.note: Visible letters are exposed alongside a full hidden copy, so screen readers repeat the text, and the flip is hover-only.

issues: Mid-flip letters show a mirrored back face overlapping their neighbours, briefly muddying the line.
polish_why: The flip has weight and staggers nicely; the mirrored mid-flight glyphs look messy for a beat.
title: Text 3D Flip
